selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What mistaken idea is the nafs blamed for in the First Warning?
questions.answer: It acts as if life in this world will last a long time or never end.

questions.question: What two short time periods are mentioned to show how uncertain life is?
questions.answer: Even reaching the next year or the next day is not guaranteed.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the real reason the nafs gets bored with worship?
questions.answer: It wrongly assumes there will always be more time later.

questions.question: How is human life described in relation to time?
questions.answer: It is short and quickly passing away.

questions.question: How much of the day is described as being spent in worship?
questions.answer: One hour out of twenty-four.

questions.question: How is that hour of worship characterized?
questions.answer: It is presented as good, manageable, gentle, and beneficial.

questions.question: What lasting benefit is connected to that act of worship?
questions.answer: It helps a person gain the true happiness of the life to come.

questions.question: What does the phrase about true happiness point toward?
questions.answer: It points toward success in the eternal life, not just temporary worldly comfort.

questions.question: How does this warning try to reform the nafs?
questions.answer: It corrects its false hope of long life and teaches it to value immediate obedience.

questions.question: Who is being addressed in the First Warning?
questions.answer: The person’s own nafs, meaning the lower self.

questions.question: Why does the speaker question whether the nafs has proof of living longer?
questions.answer: To show that it has no certainty about the future.

questions.question: What attitude toward worldly enjoyment is criticized?
questions.answer: Wanting to keep enjoying this world as if it will continue forever.

questions.question: What false assumption turns worship into something annoying for the nafs?
questions.answer: The assumption that there will always be plenty of time later.

questions.question: What is the one-hour act meant to achieve beyond this worldly life?
questions.answer: It is a means to eternal success and real happiness.

questions.question: What emotional change is expected when a person understands the truth correctly?
questions.answer: Boredom should change into sincere desire and joy.

questions.question: What words best describe the act of worship in this passage: harsh and heavy, or pleasant and merciful?
questions.answer: Pleasant and merciful.

questions.question: How should a wise person respond to the shortness of life?
questions.answer: By using time carefully and giving proper attention to worship.

questions.question: What is the first challenge made to the nafs in this warning?
questions.answer: It is challenged to prove that its life will continue.

questions.question: Why is asking for proof about tomorrow important in the argument?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that even the near future is not in human control.

questions.question: What kind of outlook makes the nafs complain?
questions.answer: A careless outlook that treats temporary life as if it were permanent.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is happening to life even while a person delays worship?
questions.answer: It is passing away and being lost.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of a single hour?
questions.answer: A small amount of time can have great spiritual value if used properly.

questions.question: Which is presented as more reasonable: chasing endless comfort in this world or worshipping for eternal benefit?
questions.answer: Worshipping for eternal benefit is presented as more reasonable.

questions.question: What is the relationship between worship and eternal life in this passage?
questions.answer: Worship is presented as a path leading to lasting happiness in the next life.
